Continuing the diphenhydramine at a lower dose and keeping the barricade perpetuates the two unsafe workarounds the plan exists to replace.

The rising glucose is a concurrent parenteral-nutrition complication that requires treatment but does not explain the electrolyte triad, and a catheter infection is not supported at this point because the client is afebrile and the insertion site is benign.
